newsitem.title: FRANCE: DMC heads for 550 mln Ffr 96 loss - paper.
newsitem.headline: DMC heads for 550 mln Ffr 96 loss - paper.

text.p: French textiles company DMC could make a loss of 550 million francs in 1996, Les Echos, which interviewed DMC chief executive Jacques Boubal, said on Friday.
The company said on Thursday it expected a considerable deterioration in its second-half result after a loss of 144 million francs in the first-half, due notably to tumbling printed fabric sales.
DMC made a net profit of three million francs in 1995.
Boubal said in Les Echos newspaper: "We should see the end of the tunnel after current restructuring at the end of 1997, start of 1998".
The newspaper said acceleration of the group's restructuring programme, which foresaw staff cuts of 1,500 between September and next summer, would result in a provision of 200 million francs.
Boubal said, however, debt was not expected to rise because of capital gains on property in Germany, the newspaper said.
It said plans to close an additional site would be revealed to staff in France and Germany on December 10.
Boubal's comments on the 1996 results were reported by the daily in an article separate from the interview itself.

In the interview, Boubal said the group had to become more international to shake off over-dependence on Europe, where it generated 77 percent of sales. He cited ties with the Cha group in Hong Kong and plans for further developments in China as well as ties in Mexico giving access to sales in North America.
"DMC is going through a serious results crisis," he was quoted as saying.

"The 14 percent fall in sales since the start of the year, which continued in the third quarter, plus the 200 million provisions for restructuring, will have a serious impact on results for 1996," he said.
Debt should be kept to about a billion francs, he said.
"Next year, we're banking an a considerable improvement in operating results, without counting on an improvement in the economic situation."
